name: Slagwash Fleece Pullover — Cropped
description: Ash-grey fleece pullover cropped just above the hip, made from recycled synthetic fiber with visible pill-texture from heavy washing. Front pocket is hand-stitched with mismatched thread in rust-orange. Soft enough for couch days, warm enough for Shelf winters when the heat cuts out.
functionality: Retains body heat well; cropped hem allows layering over thermal leggings without bulk.
what_it_says: You dress for survival and comfort, not for anyone else's opinion.
story_hooks: The rust-orange stitching on the pocket matches the thread color used by a specific Shelf collective — locals might recognize it.
Whoever owned this last left a folded note tucked inside the pocket lining.

physical_description.visual_profile: Relaxed, lived-in cropped pullover with a distinctly street-worn aesthetic. Sits just above the hip on most frames, creating a casual, accessible silhouette that reads as Sub-Tier comfortable rather than aspirational. The visible pilling and faded grey give it a broken-in charm that suggests genuine use rather than intentional distressing.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and torso with a slightly loose drape. The crop length exposes the midriff by 2-3 inches, making it a piece for layering or warm indoor spaces. Sleeve cuffs are elasticated and show minor stretching from repeated wear.
physical_description.primary_material: Recycled synthetic fleece blend — soft polyester with visible degradation characteristics. The material has a matte finish with micro-texture from washing cycles.
physical_description.texture: Heavily pilled surface throughout, particularly on the front and sleeves. The pilling is uneven and organic-looking rather than uniform, indicating authentic wear rather than design choice. Softer in high-contact areas like the interior of sleeves.
physical_description.color_scheme: Ash-grey base with overall fading toward the collar and cuffs. Rust-orange hand-stitched thread on the front pocket creates a striking accent line. No intentional pattern — the color variation is purely from wear and UV exposure.
physical_description.closures: Pullover design with no closure mechanism. Crew neck with stretched elastic binding showing slight discoloration from repeated neck contact.
distinctive_features: Hand-stitched front pocket with deliberately mismatched rust-orange embroidery thread
Visible pilling texture across entire garment surface
Cropped length ending just above natural hip bone
Slight color fade gradient from shoulders downward
Fraying at the hem from repeated washing without finishing
Interior cuff wear patterns suggesting frequent pushing-up of sleeves
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 — Ungoverned/Sub-grade working class. No branded markers. Functionality over presentation. The cost of replacement exceeds the cost of repair.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by people in the Shelf districts, maintenance workers during off-hours, or anyone prioritizing warmth over appearance. Signals someone who shops second-hand markets rather than retail. Often paired with salvage-grade tech or visible augmentation ports. This is the uniform of people who fix things, not the people who sell them.
physical_description.condition_typical: Always worn-in. Pilling is permanent. Usually paired with visible stains from work or weather. May have small repairs or patches on the back. The rust-orange stitching is often the most visible part due to contrast. Never looks 'new' — it's an item that proved durable enough to keep wearing.
